A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Transformer-based PRNG prediction study. Their main text, equations, figures, table and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original prediction experiments, scaling studies, curriculum comparisons, embedding analyses and attention-head ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds analyses of higher principal components of learned embeddings.

M1.justification: The Transformer architecture, prediction objective, tokenization, pretrained initialization and curriculum procedures are retained. Added explanations of tokenization costs do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TLCG, XSLRR, XSHRR and XSHRS under the same separate and combined settings, modulus ranges and truncation conditions. The additional embedding diagnostics introduce no new prediction task or dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Random-guessing and estimated brute-force comparisons, curriculum alternatives and initialization comparisons are retained. The newly discussed HMM studies are related work, not newly evaluated comparators.

E3.justification: The added representation diagnostics quantify correlations with signed or weighted bit statistics and compare bit-flip pairs for PC3–PC6 in Figures 24–25. Existing predictive evaluations retain their splits, metrics, model configurations and training budgets.

E4.justification: Appendix H.1.1 extends the embedding analysis beyond PC1–PC2, investigating whether higher components encode interpretable bit patterns and how much variance they explain. Existing scaling, curriculum, attention and head-ablation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 6 retains its standard-deviation shading, with no added run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or significance tests. The added PCA variance fractions characterize representations rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: New results include PC3/PC4 variance fractions of 3.2%/2.4%, PC4 correlation 0.9515 with its proposed bit statistic, and weak PC5/PC6 correlations (Appendix H.1.1, Figures 24–25). Existing prediction scores and scaling plots are unchanged.

T1.justification: The Hull–Dobell conditions, bit-period argument, generator definitions and compute derivations are retained. Added PC3/PC4 formulas describe empirical relationships rather than new formal derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the rotation-invariant clustering claim to leading principal components instead of describing the model's embeddings broadly. Claims about prediction, modulus scaling and curriculum learning remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix H.1.1 explains that the first four components cover about 15% of embedding variance and that PC5–PC6 lack simple interpretations. Section 8 explicitly identifies a full mechanistic account and cryptographically secure generators as open directions. Tokenization tradeoffs are also explained.

D1.justification: Appendix B retains the implementation settings, hyperparameters, hardware and training times. The existing code link moves from a footnote to a reproducibility statement; the added tokenization discussion explains an already documented choice.

R1.justification: Section 7 adds an HMM comparison citing Wei et al. (2022), Xie et al. (2022) and Dai et al. (2025), distinguishing their probabilistic transition tables from PCGs' deterministic algebraic structure. Existing research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction and interpretability edits, expands Appendix H.1.1, and adds Discussion, Reproducibility Statement and an LLM-use disclosure. Most prose and the original section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds two PCA figures containing four panels, relocates Figure 7 and Table 1, and renumbers original Figures 24–27 as 26–29. Conference headers and author formatting change, while existing plots are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves the precision of the embedding interpretation by examining higher components, narrowing the clustering claim and explaining the limited variance covered. Added research context and explicit mechanistic limitations also help. These are useful, bounded gains; the predictive evidence and underlying method remain unchanged.
